newsitem.title: NORWAY: Aker seeks extra pay from Hydro for Njord - report.
newsitem.headline: Aker seeks extra pay from Hydro for Njord - report.

text.p: Aker Stord, a subsidiary of Norwegian industrial group Aker ASA, seeks 518 million crowns from Norsk Hydro ASA for extra work on an offshore platform, daily Aftenposten said on Wednesday.
If Aker's claim is accepted, the price for the Njord oil platform would rise from 2.8 billion crowns to at least 3.3 billion crowns.

"It is true that we have received a demand from Aker for 518 million crowns," Aftenposten quoted Norsk Hydro spokesman Tor Steinum as saying. "But we don't think at first glance that the demand is particularly reasonable."
He said however Norsk Hydro would study Aker's claim closely before giving an answer.
Norsk Hydro awarded the contract in March last year to Aker to build the floating production system for the Njord field, on Haltenbanken off mid-Norway.

"The reason for the demand is that work has been carried out on top of the original contract, and we feel this extra work should be paid for by the Njord licensees," Aker spokesman Thorbjoern Andersen was quoted as saying.
Under the agreement, the platform must be ready by June 30 next year in order for Njord to start production in October.
The field will be developed using a semi-submersible production platform and a floating storage vessel.

Hydro has a 30-percent share in Njord while the Norwegian government, through Den norske stats Oljeselskap (Statoil) and its direct involvement, controls 50 percent. Mobil and Veba AG unit Deminex hold the remainder.
